children: Shares of J.B. Hunt Transport Services

are pinned down in Wednesday’s premarket trading and reverberating through the trucking sector after the company’s chief executive issued a warning about operational costs and profitability for the current quarter.
Speaking at Morgan Stanley’s conference last night, J.B. Hunt
CEO Brad Delco cautioned that while there is a mismatch between supply and demand for intermodal, J.B. Hunt
expects second-quarter to third-quarter earnings to drop 5% to 10%.

“There are still things to be concerned about,” Delco said. “Gas prices jumped another $0.30 this week…so we should be concerned about the consumer, but I see some of the structural challenges on driver capacity not letting up at all. If anything, it’s probably getting worse.”
Expanding on fuel costs, Delco believes the “radical and abnormal” swings in fuel prices will likely create a $10M headwind sequentially from Q2 to Q3.
Meanwhile, the higher cost of recruiting, advertising, onboarding, training, and sign-on bonuses for new drivers will add another $25M in costs in Q3 versus Q2.
Despite the cost pressure, both Delco and the company’s intermodal president, Darren Field, noted the “very strong” demand for intermodal shipping largely from the shortage of drivers.

“Any kind of highway capacity that might have been a retail supply for even a really long length of haul, what we would consider traditional intermodal is just the most expensive it’s ever been,” Field said, a dynamic that will be reflected in the days ahead as intermodal bid season for 2027 begins. This presents trucking companies with a “big opportunity” to close the gap between costs and truckload rates.
